title: The students on real tables, in shadow: DCLab's product path on real OpenML tables, recorded and measured
request: Try the students on real tables in shadow, record and store them; include Claude; then gather data for 100 students (the owner).
spec: ledger.capture.solution_saved and ledger.shadow (22.4); real_homework's derived states (29.15); the lake's split (26.2); docs/guides/STUDENTS_100_PLAN.md
plan: Run the product path on each real table, recording its decisions with every student's shadow.
Measure on the dev tables against the declared truths.
Claude's silver opinion on a sample of the disagreements, capped and kept apart.
Review; fix; restart the run in the corrected layout.

decisions.decision: Train tables in a workspace under train consent, dev tables in one with no consent, sealed tables left out.
decisions.why: A student must never be trained on what it is measured on, and a sealed set is read once.

decisions.decision: Records filed under the table (draft id), not a project.
decisions.why: A project no store knows is stamped operate; the workspace's own consent should stamp these.

decisions.decision: The proposal recorded with a rule actor.
decisions.why: Nobody chose: an agent answer would be a copy credited to the intern.

change: dclab_rnd/real_shadow.py (new), dclab_rnd/ledger/capture.py (_who: the rule keeping its proposal), tests/test_real_shadow.py, docs/guides/STUDENTS_100_PLAN.md

findings.defect: The tests needed fitted students that are not in git.
findings.scenario: A clean checkout: no shadow, the tests fail.
findings.fix: A tiny student fitted in the test.

findings.defect: silver saved empty answers as done after a failure or the cap.
findings.scenario: A failing transport: three lines with claude null, no stop.
findings.fix: Stop when its error count grows; write nothing.

findings.defect: Sealed and dev tables went into a workspace under train consent.
findings.scenario: 104 lake-sealed tables would land in the store's train split.
findings.fix: Sealed left out; dev in a workspace with no consent; train only under train consent.

findings.defect: silver used a bare gateway from the command line.
findings.scenario: No usage log, no monthly caps.

findings.defect: A lost write was marked done.
findings.scenario: A full disk during the batch: the table never retried.
findings.fix: DROPPED counted before and after; no marker when it grew.

findings.defect: Answers credited to a rule and an agent that did not give them.
findings.scenario: roles under rule:prepare_roles; the proposal as the intern's.
findings.cause: Labels copied from the engine path.

findings.defect: measure hid abstentions and mixed students.
findings.scenario: Accuracy over answered decisions only; two students pooled.
findings.cause: Records without a shadow dropped; one key per point.
findings.fix: Coverage counted; keyed by point and student.

findings.scenario: A passing timeout drops a dev table.

findings.defect: A stopped run could record a table twice.
findings.scenario: Ctrl-C inside batch, then a rerun.
findings.cause: The batch writes in finally, no marker.
findings.fix: One record per point, table and subject in _rows.

findings.defect: The tests did not prove the claims.
findings.scenario: Truth path, cap, non-empty answers, failure path untested.

findings.defect: The run was killed on its second real table.
findings.cause: dclab_core.analyse built every combination of the categories.

findings.defect: Claude's silver answers were cut at the token limit.
findings.scenario: 7 of 17 abstained, then three in a row: the run stopped.
findings.cause: max_tokens 200 for an answer and a one-sentence reason.
findings.fix: 600 tokens; a failed request tried once more, kept as a failed abstention, asked again on the next run.

findings.defect: A request refused near the cap was kept as a failed answer.
findings.scenario: The cap test after the 600-token change.
findings.cause: The cap check looked at the spend only, not the next request's cost.
findings.fix: Stop when what is left is under 1.5 times the costliest answer so far.

measurements.name: the real-table shadow run
measurements.gate: every table done or failed with its reason; dev tables measured only
measurements.result: 652 tables, 50,967 decisions, 0 failed; roles: rule 93.6%, invented student 94.0%, real-homework student 99.7%; identifier: rule 100%, 98.9%, 99.2%; Claude sides with the rule on 95 of 100 leakage disagreements
limits: the tables' declarations are their uploaders'
Claude's opinion is silver, not truth

outcome: On real tables the invented-only students are not better than the rules; with real homework the column-role student reaches 99.7% against the rule's 93.6%.
lessons: Running on real data found a crash invented data never would.
A measurement workspace must not share consent with a training one.
risks: The tables' declarations are their uploaders'.
